signals.ai_share_evidence: No AI-attribution trailers or bot authors in any of the 31 commits (2024-08 to 2024-11); informal human commit style ('save', 'bump version') and an external human contributor PR; nothing observable indicates AI authorship.

evidence.excerpt: Root: manifest.json (917 B), background.js (3927 B), content.js (3229 B), popup/ (dir), utils/ (dir), images/ (dir), privacy_policy.md (1521 B), Makefile — a complete unpacked Chrome extension matching the README install flow.

Feature commits back README claims: 0b486c0 'handle artifacts and attachments', 4b39a03 'save to clipboard button', 1f74f8b 'handle conversation edits', f0e516a merge of 'use-storage' branch (PAT stored via extension storage), afd1759 external contributor Alex Strick van Linschoten.
Metadata: 'A Chrome extension that saves conversations with Claude to GitHubGists or your clipboard.', language JavaScript, stargazers_count 94, forks_count 8, commit_count 31, contributors 2.
'Obtain a personal access token (PAT) with the gist scope ... After installing the extension, you can click the extension icon to save your PAT.'

counter_evidence.excerpt: 16 of 31 commit messages are the uninformative word 'save' (e.g. fffed4d, 63836c4, b73eeda, 2024-08 to 2024-11), which superficially resembles low-effort dumping; counter: substantive feature commits are interleaved (4b39a03 'save to clipboard button', 0b486c0 'handle artifacts and attachments', 1f74f8b 'handle conversation edits', storage-based PAT via f0e516a), an external contributor's PR was merged (afd1759), and privacy_policy.md ships with the extension.

counter_evidence_review.outcome: Terse messages reflect informal solo iteration over four months, not mass generation; the artifact set is a coherent working extension and README claims are backed by named feature commits.

notes: Small, genuine Chrome extension for exporting Claude conversations to Gists or clipboard; user supplies their own gist-scoped PAT and storage-based handling is visible in the merged 'use-storage' branch, with no secrets shipped in the repo. Chrome-extension scaffolding (manifest/background/content/popup) accounts for the moderate boilerplate share. Weakest area is documentation depth: no limitations or tradeoff discussion, and many commits are just labeled 'save'.
